analysis: What changed vs the 9 AM brief: Monday's Huang-led rally is now unwinding in full. Tuesday gave back part of the surge (Nasdaq -1.48%, chips -7.9%) while the Dow closed above 50,000 for the first time, and overnight the tape turned down again — Nasdaq futures -2.22% at 4:32 AM ET — on reports of new Section 301 tariffs on 16 trading partners. The overnight catalyst is trade, but the fragility predates it: Nvidia is -4.9% premarket and on track for its worst month since 2022 despite a blowout Nov 17 quarter, and Anthropic has slipped to ~$77 premarket, well under its $83 IPO price, with its market cap near $1.02T. The sharpest tension in the tape is Dell vs the chips: Dell just printed a record quarter (revenue +103%, AI backlog $132.3B) and raised its full-year guide to $202B, yet AI hardware stocks keep falling — the market is pricing governance, probes and valuation, not a demand collapse. The same bar showed up after the close: Workday, Autodesk and Ambarella all beat and fell anyway, Ambarella -38% on a weak guide. Rotation is the other half of the story: value and health care led Tuesday (9 of 11 sectors green, Dow +0.85%) while tech lagged. Signal vs noise: the tariff reports (single-source, no rates published yet), the Anthropic slide below IPO, and the beat-and-fall earnings pattern are signal; the exact premarket percentages and the Dow's round-number milestone are noise. Today's deciding input is the 8:30 AM ET data dump — PCE, Q3 GDP revision, durable goods — into a thin Thanksgiving-week tape.

community_signals.takeaway: Thread adds nuance the headlines skip: commenters distinguish legal Malaysia hosting of Nvidia chips from the alleged smuggling into Chinese data centers, flag sloppy reporting that conflated the two, and debate whether Huang's governance issues (affairs, board conflict) or the export-control probes are the real driver — a useful check on the 'proven complicity' framing in some coverage.
community_signals.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: Futures point to a gap-down open: at 4:32 AM ET, Dow E-minis -377 pts (-0.75%), S&P 500 E-minis -94.5 pts (-1.31%), Nasdaq 100 E-minis -584.25 pts (-2.22%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The overnight slide extends Tuesday's tech giveback into a second day — the open is set to start well below Tuesday's close, with tech leading the downside.

headlines.headline: Trump administration poised to unveil new tariffs on 16 major trading partners after a Section 301 probe into excess industrial capacity; findings expected as soon as Tuesday/Wednesday, with no final rates or product lists published yet. Existing deal caps (15% EU/Japan/South Korea, 19% Malaysia, 20% China while the truce holds) are expected to be honored.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile: Reuters cites three anonymous sources and USTR/White House did not respond. If real, it is the overnight catalyst for the futures slide and a fresh US-China friction headwind for the AI complex.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -4.9% premarket, extending Tuesday's -5.86% close at $155.38; on track for its worst month since 2022, down ~24% in November. Bank of America cut its target to $280 from $350 and Oppenheimer to $250 from $315; retail dip buyers who bought Nov 4-24 are barely breaking even on average (Vanda Research via SPI Asset Management).
headlines.why_it_matters: The reinstatement rally is being retraced fast despite strong fundamentals — earnings context: Nov 17, EPS $2.68 vs $2.47 expected, revenue $115.84B vs $109.28B expected (+103% y/y). The overhangs (SEC probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Huang's Dec 1 House testimony) still dominate the tape.

headlines.headline: Anthropic -5.6% premarket to ~$77.31, putting its market cap near $1.02T; it closed Tuesday at $81.91, below its $83 IPO price, after touching a $75.61 low. Form 4 filings show CEO Dario Amodei sold 3.72M shares and President Daniela Amodei 3.8M shares since the IPO.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade's newest public name is now well under water vs its IPO price within a week — the cooling is spreading from hardware to AI software names and poisoning sentiment for the whole complex.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps all red premarket (6:22 AM ET): Alphabet -2.96%, Amazon -2.88%, Tesla -2.31%, Microsoft -1.83%, Meta -1.13%, Apple -0.51%.
headlines.why_it_matters: No mega-cap is escaping the premarket slide — the least AI-exposed name (Apple) is down least, which keeps the rotation-into-value pattern from Tuesday intact.

headlines.headline: Dell crushed Q3 FY27 after the close: revenue $54.94B, +103% y/y, vs $49.32B expected; adjusted EPS $9.45 vs $6.59 expected. AI-optimized server revenue $22B (+291%), AI backlog a record $132.3B, full-year revenue guide raised to $202B from $192B, plus a $25B buyback expansion. Shares +2-3% after hours after closing -11.83% Tuesday at $295.28.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuine demand-side counterweight: AI server demand is booming on the numbers even as AI stocks fall — the selloff is about governance, probes and valuation, not a demand collapse.

headlines.headline: Beat-and-fall after the close: Workday beat (EPS $2.82 vs $2.45, revenue $2.71B vs $2.69B) but fell ~7% on a lighter Q4 subscription guide; Autodesk beat (EPS $3.20 vs $2.91, revenue $2.16B) but fell ~4%; Ambarella guided Q4 to $70-75M vs ~$112M expected and crashed ~38%; HP beat (EPS $0.83 vs $0.74, revenue $16.0B) and was roughly flat.
headlines.why_it_matters: Five beats, five falls — the market is judging guidance, not the quarter, and the bar for high-multiple tech is higher than a beat alone clears.

headlines.headline: Chip selloff broadens beyond AI names: Texas Instruments fell -11.25% Tuesday to $258.44 (after a +10.4% Monday on a Cantor Fitzgerald upgrade) and is -2.34% premarket at $252.40; Analog Devices fell -17.37% Tuesday, Micron -11.01%.
headlines.why_it_matters: Analog and memory names are falling with the AI complex — the unwind is sector-wide, not a single-name Nvidia story.

headlines.headline: Today's data dump at 8:30 AM ET: October PCE inflation (the Fed's preferred gauge), Q3 GDP second estimate, and durable goods — the last big data before Thanksgiving. Rate futures price a ~97.8% chance of a 25bp December hike; FOMC minutes (Nov 18) showed nearly all officials expect a December hike, and NY Fed President Williams said Monday the Fed still has 'work to do' on inflation.
headlines.why_it_matters: PCE is the day's deciding input — a hot print would harden the hawkish path into December and add pressure to an already fragile tape; a soft one could steady it.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) — revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M, DCF $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Nov 24 Zacks analysis highlights the $500M order book through 2029, with >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted and revenue per horsepower +8% y/y. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027. WTI $81.63 (+1.82%) is a modest tailwind for the energy complex.
